title: Avoiding Arc<T> with Complex Unsafe Raw Pointer Sharing
pattern: Using unsafe raw pointers (`*const T`, `*mut T`) instead of safe thread-safe reference-counted pointers (`std::sync::Arc<T>`) to "avoid atomic reference counting overhead."
why_bad: Atomic reference increments only occur on pointer cloning. Bypassing `Arc` with raw pointers bypasses Rust's safety guarantees entirely, leading to catastrophic dangling pointers and data races, with zero profiled performance differences [317].
detection: Replacing standard safe pointer structures with unsafe raw pointers in multithreaded sharing contexts under the guise of performance.
counterexample: Extremely tight lock-free implementation internals where node pointers are reclaimed using proven epoch structures. `Contextual`.
fix: Use the safe, atomic, thread-safe reference-counted pointer `std::sync::Arc<T>`.
